terms.definition: The part of an app that people see and use, such as web pages in a browser.
terms.example: The frontend is the web shop page where a customer picks Rice 50kg and sees the price in FCFA.

terms.definition: The part of a system that runs on a server: it stores data, applies business rules and answers requests.
terms.example: The backend checks that Mile 4 really has 12 bags of rice before it accepts an order.

terms.definition: Application Programming Interface: an agreed way for one program to ask another program for data or actions.
terms.example: The web shop calls the Nkwen API to get every product with its stock at Bafoussam Centre.

terms.definition: A window where you type commands for the computer instead of clicking.
terms.example: In the terminal, type node hello.js to run your first Nkwen program.

terms.definition: A program that runs JavaScript outside the browser, for example in your terminal or on a server.
terms.example: node restock.js uses Node.js to print which Nkwen products need restocking.

terms.definition: A system setting listing the folders where the computer looks for programs you type in the terminal.
terms.example: If 'node' is not recognized, Node.js is missing from PATH; reinstall and tick Add to PATH.

terms.definition: The programming language that runs in every web browser; with Node.js it also runs on computers and servers.
terms.example: JavaScript calculates the basket total when a customer adds two bags of Rice 50kg.

terms.definition: A name that stores a value so your program can use or change it later.
terms.example: let stock = 12; stores the number of rice bags left at the Nkwen branch.

terms.definition: A JavaScript keyword that creates a variable you cannot reassign. Use let when the value must change.
terms.example: const VAT_RATE = 0.1925; the VAT rate never changes while the till runs.

terms.definition: The kind of value something is, such as a number, a string of text or true/false.
terms.example: 35000 is a number, 'Rice 50kg' is a string, and inStock = true is a boolean.

terms.definition: Code that repeats, for example once for every item in a list.
terms.example: A loop visits each product and prints a restock alert for every one below its level.

terms.definition: An ordered list of values in one variable. Items are counted from 0.
terms.example: products[0] is the first product in the Nkwen array, Rice 50kg.

terms.definition: A group of named values (keys and values) that describes one thing.
terms.example: { name: 'Rice 50kg', price: 35000, stock: 12 } is one product object.

terms.definition: Text in a program, written between quotes.
terms.example: 'Commercial Avenue' is a string holding a branch name.

terms.definition: Plain-language steps that describe a solution before you write real code.
terms.example: Pseudocode: for each product, if stock is at or below the reorder level, add it to the alert list.

terms.definition: An unusual input at the limits, such as zero, empty or the exact boundary, that often breaks code.
terms.example: Stock exactly equal to the reorder level is an edge case: does it trigger a restock alert?

terms.definition: A tool that records the history of your files, so you can save versions, go back and work with others.
terms.example: Git keeps every saved version of the Nkwen restock program, with who changed what.

terms.definition: A website that stores Git repositories online so you can share code, review it and work as a team.
terms.example: Your Nkwen calculator lives on GitHub, where your mentor can read every commit.

terms.definition: A project folder tracked by Git, with its full history of changes.
terms.example: The innova-software-engineering repository holds all your chapter folders and their history.

terms.definition: A saved snapshot of your changes in Git, with a message saying what changed.
terms.example: git commit -m "Add restock alerts for low stock" saves today's work.

terms.definition: The Git command that sends your local commits to the remote copy, such as GitHub.
terms.example: After committing, git push puts your Nkwen work on GitHub for your mentor.

terms.definition: The first file people read in a repository: it explains what the project is and how to run it.
terms.example: The README says how to run the Nkwen calculator and what each file does.

terms.definition: A mistake in code that makes it do the wrong thing.
terms.example: A bug made the basket add VAT twice, so Rice 50kg cost too much.

terms.definition: Finding out why code goes wrong and fixing it.
terms.example: Debugging showed the total was wrong because price was the string '35000', not a number.

terms.definition: A named block of code that does one job. You call it, often give it inputs and get a result.
terms.example: lineTotal(price, quantity) returns 70000 for two bags of rice at 35000 FCFA.

terms.definition: A named input in a function's definition.
terms.example: In function lineTotal(price, quantity), price and quantity are parameters.

terms.definition: A JavaScript command that prints a value to the terminal or browser console.
terms.example: console.log(total) prints 70000 so you can check the basket total.

terms.definition: A way to answer interview questions: Situation, Task, Action, Result.
terms.example: STAR: the Mile 4 stock was wrong (S), I had to fix it (T), I added tests (A), errors stopped (R).

terms.definition: When another developer reads your changes before they are merged, to catch problems and share knowledge.
terms.example: In code review, your partner spots that the discount is applied before VAT instead of after.

terms.definition: A request on GitHub to merge one branch into another, where the team discusses and reviews the changes.
terms.example: Open a pull request from add-search into main so your partner can review the Nkwen search.

terms.definition: JavaScript Object Notation: a text format for data made of objects and lists. APIs usually send JSON.
terms.example: {"name": "Rice 50kg", "price": 35000} is one product in JSON.

terms.definition: The position of an item in an array, counted from 0; in a database, a lookup structure that speeds up searches.
terms.example: products[2] gets the item at index 2, the third Nkwen product.

terms.definition: A function you pass to another function so it can call it later.
terms.example: products.filter(p => p.stock === 0) passes a callback that tests each product.

terms.definition: An array method that makes a new array by changing every item with a callback.
terms.example: products.map(p => p.name) gives a list of all Nkwen product names.

terms.definition: An array method that keeps only the items for which a callback returns true.
terms.example: products.filter(p => p.stock === 0) lists every product that is out of stock.

terms.definition: An array method that combines all items into one value, such as a total.
terms.example: items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.price * i.qty, 0) gives the basket total in FCFA.

terms.definition: A whole number with no decimal part. Store FCFA amounts as integers to avoid rounding errors.
terms.example: 35000 FCFA is stored as the integer 35000, never 35000.5.

terms.definition: The list printed with an error showing which functions were running, and the file and line of each.
terms.example: The stack trace points to basket.js line 14, where the price was read.

terms.definition: In a debugger, a line where the program pauses so you can inspect values. In CSS, a screen width where the layout changes.
terms.example: Put a breakpoint on the VAT line and check the total before tax is added.

terms.definition: A small automatic check that one function gives the expected result.
terms.example: A unit test checks that lineTotal(35000, 2) returns 70000.

terms.definition: A test that checks several parts working together, such as screens, code and storage.
terms.example: An integration test taps Add to order on a phone and checks the basket shows Rice 50kg.

terms.definition: Testing or following a whole user journey from start to finish, through every part of the system.
terms.example: End-to-end: a customer orders on the web shop and the manager sees the order in the API.

terms.definition: An organised store of data that a program can search and change safely, often shared by many users.
terms.example: The Nkwen database holds every product, branch, order and stock level.

terms.definition: HyperText Markup Language: the code that gives a web page its structure, such as headings, paragraphs and links.
terms.example:
Nkwen Traders

is HTML for the main heading of the shop page.

terms.definition: Cascading Style Sheets: the code that styles a web page, such as colours, spacing and layout.
terms.example: CSS turns the Nkwen product list into neat cards with green prices.

terms.definition: One piece of an HTML page, made by a tag and its content.
terms.example:
Rice 50kg: 36,005 FCFA

is a paragraph element.

terms.definition: In HTML and CSS, a label for styling elements. In PHP and Dart, a blueprint for creating objects.
terms.example: <span class="low"> marks low stock; CSS colours every .low item red.

terms.definition: A CSS layout tool that arranges items in a row or column and shares space between them.
terms.example: Flexbox puts the logo left and the branch menu right in the Nkwen header.

terms.definition: A CSS layout tool that places items in rows and columns at the same time.
terms.example: CSS Grid shows one product card per row on a phone and three on a laptop.

terms.definition: Building pages that adapt to any screen size, from a small phone to a large monitor.
terms.example: With responsive design, the Nkwen catalogue is readable on a 360px-wide phone.

terms.definition: A CSS rule that applies styles only when the screen matches a condition, such as a minimum width.
terms.example: @media (min-width: 768px) shows two product columns on tablets.

terms.definition: Designing and writing CSS for small phone screens first, then adding rules for bigger screens.
terms.example: Mobile-first: write the one-column catalogue, then add a media query for laptops.

terms.definition: A short text description of an image, read by screen readers and shown if the image fails to load.
terms.example: alt="Bag of Rice 50kg" tells a blind customer what the picture shows.

terms.definition: Making apps usable by everyone, including people using screen readers, keyboards or small screens.
terms.example: Accessibility: the Nkwen basket can be used with only a keyboard.

terms.definition: A tool in Chrome DevTools that scores a page for performance, accessibility and good practice.
terms.example: Lighthouse gave the Nkwen page 72 for accessibility until you added labels.

terms.definition: Tools built into the browser to inspect a page's HTML, CSS, network requests and errors.
terms.example: Open DevTools, then the Network tab, to see the request for the product list.

terms.definition: A web address, such as https://example.com/products?branch=nkwen.
terms.example: The URL /products?branch=mile4 asks for products at the Mile 4 branch.

terms.definition: A short need written from a user's view: As a ..., I want ..., so that ...
terms.example: As a customer in Bafoussam, I want to see stock at my branch, so that I don't travel for nothing.

terms.definition: To put your app on a server so real users can reach it.
terms.example: Deploy the Nkwen API so the web shop can call it from anywhere.

terms.definition: The real reason a problem happens, not just its visible symptom.
terms.example: The root cause was a price stored as text, not the wrong total on screen.

terms.definition: Document Object Model: the browser's live tree of a page's elements, which JavaScript can read and change.
terms.example: JavaScript changes the DOM to show 'Out of stock' under Rice 50kg without reloading.

terms.definition: A JavaScript method that finds the first element matching a CSS selector.
terms.example: document.querySelector('#basket-total') finds the element showing the basket total.

terms.definition: Something that happens on a page, such as a click, a key press or a form being sent.
terms.example: Clicking Add to basket fires a click event for Rice 50kg.

terms.definition: Tells an element to run a function each time a chosen event happens.
terms.example: button.addEventListener('click', addToBasket) adds rice to the basket on every click.

terms.definition: The data an app is showing right now. When state changes, the screen is drawn again from it.
terms.example: The state holds the chosen branch, the search text and the basket items.

terms.definition: A property that reads or replaces an element's HTML. Unsafe with user text, because it can run scripts.
terms.example: Never put a customer's review into innerHTML; use textContent instead.

terms.definition: Browser storage that keeps small pieces of text on the device, even after the page is closed.
terms.example: The basket is saved in localStorage, so it is still there after a refresh.

terms.definition: Cross-site scripting: an attack where someone's text is run as code in other users' browsers.
terms.example: A product review containing <script> could cause XSS if shown with innerHTML.

terms.definition: A program that sends requests to a server, such as a browser or a mobile app.
terms.example: The rep app is a client: it asks the Nkwen server for today's products.

terms.definition: A computer or program that waits for requests and sends back answers.
terms.example: The Nkwen server answers GET /products with every product and its stock.

terms.definition: Domain Name System: the internet's phone book that turns domain names into IP addresses.
terms.example: DNS tells your phone which server hosts the Nkwen Traders site.

terms.definition: HyperText Transfer Protocol: the rules browsers, apps and servers use to send requests and responses.
terms.example: The web shop sends an HTTP request to the API and gets the product list back.

terms.definition: HTTP made secure with encryption, so others on the network cannot read or change the data.
terms.example: Login and Mobile Money pages must use HTTPS, never plain HTTP.

terms.definition: The top part of a page or table. In HTTP, extra information sent with a request or response, such as Content-Type.
terms.example: The header Accept: application/json asks the Nkwen API to answer in JSON.

terms.definition: A three-digit number in a response that says how the request went, such as 200, 404 or 500.
terms.example: Status code 201 means the order for Rice 50kg was created.

terms.definition: The HTTP method for reading data without changing anything.
terms.example: GET /products/12 reads the details of Rice 50kg.

terms.definition: The HTTP method for sending data to create something new, such as an order.
terms.example: POST /orders creates an order for 2 bags of Rice 50kg at Mile 4.

terms.definition: The HTTP method for changing only part of a resource.
terms.example: PATCH /orders/7 with {"status": "delivered"} changes only the order's status.

terms.definition: The HTTP method for removing a resource.
terms.example: DELETE /products/12 removes Rice 50kg from the catalogue.

terms.definition: The status code meaning Not Found: the thing you asked for does not exist.
terms.example: GET /products/999 answers 404 because Nkwen has no product 999.

terms.definition: The status code meaning Unprocessable Content: the request was understood but the data broke a rule.
terms.example: An order with quantity -3 gets 422 and a message saying which field is wrong.

terms.definition: The status code meaning Conflict: the request clashes with the current state, such as too little stock.
terms.example: Ordering 20 bags when Mile 4 has 12 gets 409: not enough stock.

terms.definition: The status code meaning Unauthorized: you are not logged in, or your token is missing or wrong.
terms.example: Calling /api/me with no token answers 401.

terms.definition: The status code meaning Forbidden: you are logged in but not allowed to do this.
terms.example: A cashier who tries to change prices gets 403; only managers may.

terms.definition: Code that starts a slow task, such as a network call, and carries on without waiting for it.
terms.example: Fetching products is asynchronous, so the page stays usable while they load.

terms.definition: A JavaScript object for a result that will arrive later; it is pending, then fulfilled or rejected.
terms.example: fetch() returns a promise that later gives the response with Nkwen products.

terms.definition: A keyword that marks a function as asynchronous, so it can use await and always returns a promise or Future.
terms.example: async function loadProducts() fetches the Nkwen catalogue.

terms.definition: A keyword that pauses an async function until a promise or Future finishes, then gives its result.
terms.example: const res = await fetch('/products'); waits for the product list.

terms.definition: The browser's built-in function for sending HTTP requests from JavaScript.
terms.example: fetch('/products?branch=nkwen') asks the API for Nkwen branch stock.

terms.definition: The part of a URL after ?, holding name=value pairs separated by &.
terms.example: In /products?branch=mile4&category=grains, the query string has two filters.

terms.definition: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing: browser rules that decide if a page from one site may call an API on another.
terms.example: The API must allow the web shop's address in CORS, or the browser blocks its requests.

terms.definition: The live system that real users use, as opposed to test or development copies.
terms.example: In production, debug mode must be off so customers never see error details.

terms.definition: A message a service sends to your server's URL when something happens, such as a payment finishing.
terms.example: When the customer approves, the payment provider's webhook tells the Nkwen API the order is paid.

terms.definition: One URL plus HTTP method that an API offers, such as GET /products.
terms.example: POST /orders is the endpoint for creating an order.

terms.definition: A command-line tool for sending HTTP requests, handy for testing APIs.
terms.example: curl http://localhost:8000/api/products shows the Nkwen products as JSON.

terms.definition: Scrambling data so only someone with the right key can read it; it can be reversed with that key.
terms.example: HTTPS encryption stops anyone on the café Wi-Fi from reading your MoMo PIN.

terms.definition: Deciding what a logged-in user is allowed to do.
terms.example: Authorization lets a branch manager change Mile 4 stock but not Bafoussam's.

terms.definition: Checking who a user is, for example with a password or token.
terms.example: Authentication checks that the email and password really belong to cashier Ngwa.

terms.definition: A secret string the server gives after login, which the app sends to prove who it is.
terms.example: The rep app sends its token with each request, so the API knows which rep is calling.

terms.definition: Combining the changes from one branch into another.
terms.example: Merge the add-search branch into main once the review is approved.

terms.definition: When two branches change the same lines and Git cannot decide which version to keep.
terms.example: Both partners changed the VAT line, so Git shows a merge conflict for you to resolve.

terms.definition: GitHub rules that stop changes reaching a branch unless checks pass and someone approves.
terms.example: Branch protection on main means every Nkwen change needs one approval first.

terms.definition: A fixed-length fingerprint made from data that cannot be turned back. Git names commits by hash; passwords are stored hashed.
terms.example: Commit a3f9c1e is identified by its hash; the cashier's password is stored only as a hash.

terms.definition: Structured Query Language: the language for asking a database questions and changing its data.
terms.example: SQL can find every Nkwen order over 50,000 FCFA in one line.

terms.definition: Data arranged in rows and columns. In a database, each table holds one kind of thing, such as products or orders.
terms.example: The products table has one row per product, with columns for name, price and stock.

terms.definition: One line across a table. In a database table, each row is one record, such as one order.
terms.example: One row in orders: order 7, Mile 4, Rice 50kg, quantity 2.

terms.definition: One line down a table or page layout. In a database, a column holds the same kind of value for every row.
terms.example: The price column holds every Nkwen product's price in FCFA.

terms.definition: The SQL command that reads data from tables.
terms.example: SELECT name, price FROM products; lists every Nkwen product and price.

terms.definition: The part of a SQL query that keeps only rows matching a condition.
terms.example: WHERE branch = 'Mile 4' keeps only Mile 4 orders.

terms.definition: SQL that combines rows from two tables where a column matches.
terms.example: JOIN branches ON orders.branch_id = branches.id adds the branch name to each order.

terms.definition: The agreed description of an API: its endpoints, inputs, outputs and errors, which both sides must follow.
terms.example: The API contract says POST /orders answers 409 when a branch lacks stock.

terms.definition: In an API, a thing you can read or change through a URL, such as a product or an order.
terms.example: /orders/7 is the URL of one order resource.

terms.definition: Making a request safe to repeat. An Idempotency-Key header lets the server spot and ignore a repeated request.
terms.example: The rep app resends an order with the same Idempotency-Key, and only one order is created.

terms.definition: An action is idempotent if repeating it gives the same result as doing it once.
terms.example: PUT is idempotent: sending the same Rice 50kg price twice leaves one price.

terms.definition: Gaining one thing by giving up another, such as speed for simplicity.
terms.example: Saving orders on the phone first is a trade-off: it works offline but needs syncing later.

terms.definition: A programming language that runs on web servers; Laravel is written in it.
terms.example: The Nkwen API is written in PHP with the Laravel framework.

terms.definition: PHP's package manager: it downloads the libraries a project needs, listed in composer.json.
terms.example: composer install downloads Laravel and every library the Nkwen API uses.

terms.definition: A popular PHP framework for building web apps and APIs, with routing, database tools and testing built in.
terms.example: Laravel lets you build the Nkwen products API in a few files.

terms.definition: A ready-made structure for building apps: it calls your code and handles common jobs for you.
terms.example: Laravel is the framework; you only write the Nkwen routes, rules and models.

terms.definition: Laravel's command-line tool for creating files, running migrations, tests and the dev server.
terms.example: php artisan serve starts the Nkwen API on your laptop.

terms.definition: A rule linking a URL and HTTP method to the code that answers it.
terms.example: The route GET /api/products runs the controller that lists Nkwen products.

terms.definition: Laravel code that defines a route answering GET requests.
terms.example: Route::get('/products', [ProductController::class, 'index']); lists all products.

terms.definition: A class that holds the code answering a group of related routes.
terms.example: ProductController has index() to list products and show() to return one.

terms.definition: A file that describes a change to the database structure, so every copy of the database can be built the same way.
terms.example: A migration creates the products table with name, price and stock columns.

terms.definition: Checking that incoming data follows the rules before using it.
terms.example: Validation refuses an order with quantity 0 and answers 422.

terms.definition: Filling many model fields at once from request data. Laravel blocks fields you did not allow, such as role.
terms.example: Mass assignment protection stops a user from sending role=manager when signing up.

terms.definition: Code that runs before or after every request on a route, for example to check login.
terms.example: Auth middleware refuses any request to /api/orders that has no valid token.

terms.definition: In Laravel, a test that sends a real request to your app and checks the full response.
terms.example: A feature test posts an order and checks the answer is 201 and stock drops.

terms.definition: A setting kept outside the code, such as a password or API address, that changes per computer or server.
terms.example: DB_PASSWORD is an environment variable, different on your laptop and the live server.

terms.definition: The file holding a project's environment variables. Never commit it: it contains secrets.
terms.example: The .env file holds the MoMo key; .gitignore keeps it off GitHub.

terms.definition: The planned structure of a database or data: its tables, columns, types and links.
terms.example: The schema has products, branches and a stock table linking them.

terms.definition: A JavaScript library for building user interfaces from components.
terms.example: The Nkwen shop is rebuilt in React, with one component per product card.

terms.definition: Node.js's package manager: it installs JavaScript libraries and runs project scripts.
terms.example: npm install gets React; npm run dev starts the Nkwen shop locally.

terms.definition: A reusable piece of UI, written as a function that returns what to show.
terms.example: <ProductCard /> is a component used once for every Nkwen product.

terms.definition: HTML-like syntax inside JavaScript that React turns into elements.
terms.example:
{product.name}

is JSX that shows 'Rice 50kg'.

terms.definition: A value passed from a parent component to a child component. A child must not change its props.
terms.example: <ProductCard name="Rice 50kg" price={35000} /> passes two props.

terms.definition: A React hook that gives a component a piece of state and a function to change it.
terms.example: const [basket, setBasket] = useState([]); starts with an empty basket.

terms.definition: Code that chooses which page or screen to show for a URL or route.
terms.example: The router shows ProductPage for /products/12 and BasketPage for /basket.

terms.definition: JavaScript with types added. A checker finds mistakes before the code runs.
terms.example: TypeScript warns you when price is a string instead of a number.

terms.definition: A tool that reads your code and reports places where values have the wrong type.
terms.example: The type checker flags product.prise as a typo before you open the browser.

terms.definition: A TypeScript type that can be one of several options, written with |.
terms.example: type Branch = 'nkwen' | 'mile4' | 'commercial' | 'bafoussam';

terms.definition: A React hook for running code after the screen updates, such as fetching data.
terms.example: useEffect fetches Nkwen products when the branch changes.

terms.definition: The list given to useEffect saying which values make the effect run again.
terms.example: [branch] as the dependency array refetches stock whenever the branch changes.

terms.definition: A web app that loads once and then changes screens with JavaScript, without full page reloads.
terms.example: The Nkwen shop is a single-page app: moving to the basket needs no reload.

terms.definition: A function that takes the current state and an action, and returns the new state.
terms.example: The basket reducer handles 'add', 'remove' and 'clear' actions.

terms.definition: A bug where the result depends on which of two things finishes first.
terms.example: Two cashiers sell the last bag of rice at once; without a lock, both sales succeed.

terms.definition: A short fixed period, often one or two weeks, in which a team builds an agreed set of work.
terms.example: In Sprint 1, the squad builds ordering for Nkwen and Mile 4.

terms.definition: The programming language used to write Flutter apps.
terms.example: The rep app's price formatting is written in Dart.

terms.definition: Google's toolkit for building mobile apps for Android and iOS from one Dart codebase.
terms.example: The Nkwen sales-rep app is built with Flutter.

terms.definition: In Flutter, every piece of the screen, from text and buttons to layouts, is a widget.
terms.example: ProductCard is a widget showing Rice 50kg and its price.

terms.definition: Dart rules that stop a variable from being null unless its type allows it, catching crashes early.
terms.example: With null safety, String? phone may be null but String name never is.

terms.definition: A value meaning 'nothing here' or 'unknown'. JavaScript and Dart write null; SQL writes NULL.
terms.example: customer.phone is null when Nkwen has no phone number for that customer.

terms.definition: Dart's object for a result that arrives later, like a JavaScript promise.
terms.example: Future<List<Product>> loadProducts() returns the Nkwen catalogue later.

terms.definition: A bundle of ready-made code you add to a project, such as a library from npm or pub.dev.
terms.example: Add the http package so the rep app can call the Nkwen API.

terms.definition: A Flutter widget with no changing data of its own; it draws only from what it is given.
terms.example: StockBadge is a StatelessWidget: it shows the stock it receives.

terms.definition: A Flutter widget that keeps its own changing state.
terms.example: The quantity stepper is a StatefulWidget that remembers 1, 2 or 3 bags.

terms.definition: In Flutter, tells a StatefulWidget its state changed so it redraws. React uses state setters similarly.
terms.example: setState(() => quantity++) shows 3 bags instead of 2.

terms.definition: A Flutter test that builds a widget and checks what it shows, without a real phone.
terms.example: A widget test checks ProductCard shows 'Rice 50kg' and '36,005 FCFA'.

terms.definition: Designing an app to work without a network, saving locally first and syncing later.
terms.example: Offline-first: the rep takes orders in a village with no signal, and they send later.

terms.definition: Bringing the data on a phone and on the server into agreement.
terms.example: When the network returns, sync sends three saved orders to the Nkwen API.

terms.definition: A database storing data in tables that link to each other through keys.
terms.example: MySQL is a relational database: orders link to branches and products.

terms.definition: A popular open-source relational database server.
terms.example: The live Nkwen API stores orders in MySQL.

terms.definition: A column whose value uniquely identifies each row in a table, often id.
terms.example: id is the primary key of products: Rice 50kg is id 12.

terms.definition: A column that points to the primary key of another table, linking the two.
terms.example: orders.branch_id is a foreign key pointing to the branches table.

terms.definition: Create, Read, Update, Delete: the four basic things you do with stored data.
terms.example: The products API offers CRUD: add, list, edit and remove products.

terms.definition: The SQL command that adds new rows to a table.
terms.example: INSERT INTO products (name, price) VALUES ('Rice 50kg', 35000);

terms.definition: The SQL command that changes existing rows.
terms.example: UPDATE stock SET quantity = 10 WHERE branch_id = 2;

terms.definition: An attack where user input is run as part of a SQL query, letting attackers read or destroy data.
terms.example: Typing ' OR 1=1 -- in the search box could reveal every order if there is SQL injection.

terms.definition: A query sent with placeholders and the values separately, so input can never become SQL code.
terms.example: A prepared statement keeps a search for Rice 50kg as data, never as code.

terms.definition: A link where one row in a table relates to many rows in another.
terms.example: One branch has many orders: a one-to-many relationship.

terms.definition: Organising tables so each fact is stored once, avoiding repeated and conflicting data.
terms.example: Normalization stores each branch's name once, not in every order row.

terms.definition: Entity-Relationship Diagram: a drawing of database tables and the links between them.
terms.example: The ERD shows branches, products, orders and the stock table between them.

terms.definition: Object-Relational Mapper: a tool that lets you work with database rows as objects in code.
terms.example: Eloquent is Laravel's ORM: Product::find(12) returns Rice 50kg.

terms.definition: Laravel's ORM; each model class matches a table and lets you query it with PHP.
terms.example: Order::with('items')->get() uses Eloquent to load orders with their items.

terms.definition: When code runs one query for a list, then one more for every item, making it very slow.
terms.example: Loading 100 orders then each branch separately makes 101 queries: the N+1 problem.

terms.definition: A group of database changes that succeed together or are all undone together.
terms.example: In a database transaction, the order is saved and stock reduced together, or neither happens.

terms.definition: Undoing changes: in a database, cancelling a transaction; in deployment, returning to the last working version.
terms.example: If saving the order fails, rollback puts Mile 4 stock back to 12.

terms.definition: Laravel's query method that puts a row lock on the rows it reads, inside a transaction.
terms.example: Stock::where('product_id', 12)->lockForUpdate()->first() locks Rice 50kg stock.

terms.definition: Random data added to each password before hashing, so the same password gives different hashes.
terms.example: Two cashiers both use 'nkwen123', but salt makes their stored hashes different.

terms.definition: A deliberately slow password-hashing method with salt built in, used by Laravel.
terms.example: Laravel stores the cashier's password as a bcrypt hash starting with $2y$.

terms.definition: A way to remember a logged-in user between requests, usually with a cookie holding a session id.
terms.example: After login, the session remembers the manager until she logs out.

terms.definition: A small piece of data a website stores in the browser and gets back with every request.
terms.example: A session cookie keeps the manager logged in to the Nkwen dashboard.

terms.definition: Laravel's package for simple API token and session login.
terms.example: Sanctum gives each Nkwen staff member a token after login.

terms.definition: Limiting how many requests someone can make in a period, to stop abuse.
terms.example: Rate limiting allows 5 login attempts a minute, then answers 429.

terms.definition: A signature made from a message and a shared secret, proving the message came from someone who knows the secret.
terms.example: The payment webhook carries an HMAC, so the API can tell it is genuine.

terms.definition: JSON Web Token: a signed token carrying data about the user. It is signed, not encrypted.
terms.example: A JWT says user 4 is a manager; anyone can read it, but nobody can change it.

terms.definition: A code made with a secret key that proves who sent data and that it was not changed.
terms.example: If someone changes the amount, the signature no longer matches and the API refuses it.

terms.definition: A token sent in the Authorization header; whoever holds it is treated as the user.
terms.example: Authorization: Bearer 3|xyz... lets the rep app call /api/orders.

terms.definition: A Laravel class with rules deciding whether a user may act on a model.
terms.example: OrderPolicy lets a manager see only her own branch's orders.

terms.definition: The user's approval an app needs before using features such as the camera or notifications.
terms.example: The app asks for camera permission only when the rep taps Take photo.

terms.definition: Attaching a digital signature to an app, proving which developer made it so updates are trusted.
terms.example: Android refuses an update to the rep app unless the signing key matches.

terms.definition: Android Package: the file you install an Android app from.
terms.example: Share the rep app's APK with the Mile 4 reps for testing.

terms.definition: The upload format for Google Play (AAB); Google builds a fitting APK for each phone from it.
terms.example: Upload the app bundle to Google Play, not the APK.

terms.definition: Clear, checkable conditions a user story must meet to be done.
terms.example: Acceptance criteria: the order is refused with 409 if the branch has too little stock.

terms.definition: The team's checklist that every piece of work must meet before it counts as finished.
terms.example: Our definition of done: tests pass, code reviewed, README updated, deployed.

terms.definition: The ordered list of work the team still wants to do.
terms.example: The backlog lists ten stories, from login to the stock report.

terms.definition: The one outcome a team commits to reach by the end of a sprint.
terms.example: Sprint goal: a customer can order Rice 50kg online and the rep app sees it.

terms.definition: A team meeting after a sprint about what went well and what to change.
terms.example: At the retrospective, the squad agreed to open smaller pull requests.

terms.definition: A simple sketch of a screen's layout, without colours or real content.
terms.example: A wireframe of the basket page shows where the total and Pay button go.

terms.definition: Continuous integration: every push automatically runs the tests, so problems are found early.
terms.example: CI runs all Nkwen tests on each pull request and blocks the merge if one fails.

terms.definition: Continuous deployment: changes that pass all checks go live automatically.
terms.example: With CD, the Nkwen API deploys itself after CI passes on main.

terms.definition: A series of automatic steps, such as install, test and deploy, run on each change.
terms.example: The pipeline installs packages, runs tests, then deploys the API.

terms.definition: GitHub's built-in service for running CI and other automatic workflows.
terms.example: GitHub Actions runs php artisan test on every pull request.

terms.definition: A test that checks an API and its clients both still follow the agreed contract.
terms.example: A contract test checks POST /orders still returns id, status and total.

terms.definition: A test that makes sure a bug that was fixed does not come back.
terms.example: After fixing the double-order bug, add a regression test for it.

terms.definition: A quick check that the most important features work after a deploy.
terms.example: Smoke test: open the shop, order one Rice 50kg, see it in the manager app.

terms.definition: Planning how the parts of a software system fit together to meet its needs.
terms.example: System design: how web shop, rep app, API and database share Nkwen orders.

terms.definition: A way to describe how an algorithm's time or memory grows as the input grows.
terms.example: Checking every order against every other order is O(n²) in Big-O.

terms.definition: A technique using two positions in a list that move towards each other or together.
terms.example: Two pointers find two prices in a sorted list that sum to 50,000 FCFA.

terms.definition: One part whose failure stops the whole system.
terms.example: One server for all four branches is a single point of failure.

terms.definition: A step-by-step method for solving a problem.
terms.example: bcrypt is a hashing algorithm designed to be slow on purpose.

terms.definition: A fast test runner for JavaScript and TypeScript projects that use Vite.
terms.example: npm test runs Vitest and checks that ProductCard shows 'Out of stock' for Rice 50kg.

terms.definition: Tools for testing screens the way a user would: find elements by their text, label or role, then act.
terms.example: Testing Library finds the 'Add to basket' button by its name, then clicks it.

terms.definition: Google's main measures of page experience: how fast the main content loads, how fast the page responds, and how stable the layout is.
terms.example: Core Web Vitals showed the Nkwen home page took 5 seconds to show its main image on 3G.

terms.definition: A React framework that adds routing, server rendering and other features for production websites.
terms.example: With Next.js, Nkwen product pages arrive as ready HTML, which helps slow phones.

terms.definition: A temporary live copy of a branch or pull request, so the team can try changes before merging.
terms.example: Open the preview deploy link on your phone to check the new basket page before merging.

terms.definition: An automatic OPTIONS request the browser sends first, asking the API whether a cross-origin request is allowed.
terms.example: Before the shop's POST /orders, the browser sends a preflight; the API must allow the shop's address.

terms.definition: Describes a test that sometimes passes and sometimes fails with no code change, often because of timing.
terms.example: The checkout test is flaky: it fails when the API answers slower than 2 seconds.

terms.definition: A tool that controls a real browser automatically to run end-to-end tests.
terms.example: Playwright opens the shop, adds Rice 50kg to the basket and checks the total is 36,005 FCFA.

terms.definition: Short for end-to-end: a test that uses the whole app like a real user, from the page through the API to the database.
terms.example: An E2E test places an order in the browser and checks Mile 4 stock went down.

terms.definition: Transport Layer Security: the encryption that puts the S in HTTPS.
terms.example: The host gives the Nkwen API a TLS certificate, so its address starts with https://.
